reasons: The cited Section 13 contains a genuine Vendor-side (Garman) indemnity — 'Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses ... due to a breach of this warranty' — tied to the IP ownership/non-interference warranty, plus the customary infringement remedies (procure right, procure equivalent, replace/modify), so the clause meets the fallback position on its material terms.

No one-way or reciprocal Customer indemnity exists, and Section 15 expressly disapplies the damages limitation to breaches of Section 13, leaving the Vendor indemnity uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap and not walk-away territory.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed (redline is identical to the original) and no counterparty comment was raised; the noted gaps (no express duty to defend/control, no refund remedy, no breach-of-law/data-breach/gross-negligence limbs, ten-day notice) are correctly characterised as sub-elements short of preferred rather than material deviations.

The failed deterministic regex ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact: the indemnity verb and the infringement trigger are separated by the notice sentence, and the rationale explains this accurately; the substance of the obligation is present in the cited text.
